tldr: MDocAgent is a novel multi-modal multi-agent RAG framework for document question answering that uses five specialized agents collaborating across parallel text and image retrieval pipelines, achieving an average improvement of 12.1% over the current state-of-the-art method M3DocRAG.
contributions: A novel multi-agent framework for DocQA that integrates specialized agents for text understanding, image understanding, critical information extraction, and answer synthesis
Two parallel RAG pipelines using ColBERTv2 for text and ColPali for images with a collaborative multi-agent architecture for cross-modal reasoning
Demonstration of significant improvements on five benchmarks: MMLongBench, LongDocURL, PaperTab, PaperText, and FetaTab
Ablation studies validating the contribution of each agent and the importance of multi-modal integration
methods: MDocAgent operates in five stages: (1) Document pre-processing extracts text via OCR and PDF parsing while preserving pages as images. (2) Multi-modal context retrieval uses ColBERTv2 to retrieve top-k text segments and ColPali to retrieve top-k visually relevant pages. (3) A general agent generates an initial response from combined modalities, and a critical agent extracts key information for specialized agents. (4) A text agent and image agent perform focused analysis within their respective modalities guided by the critical information. (5) A summarizing agent integrates all agent outputs to produce the final answer. The framework uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the base model for the text agent and Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct for the other four agents.
results: MDocAgent outperforms all baselines across five benchmarks. With top-1 retrieval, it achieves 0.399 on PaperText (surpassing M3DocRAG by 16.7%) and 0.600 on FetaTab (exceeding the second-best by 21.0%). Compared to the best LVLM (Qwen2.5-VL-7B), MDocAgent shows an average improvement of 51.9%, and compared to text-RAG baseline (ColBERTv2+Llama-3.1-8B), an average improvement of 23.7%. It outperforms M3DocRAG by 12.1% on average with top-1 retrieval and by 10.9% with top-4 retrieval. With top-4 retrieval, MDocAgent outperforms Qwen2.5-VL-7B by an average of 73.5%. Ablation studies confirm that removing either the text or image agent results in noticeable performance drops.
limitations: Processing entire documents directly can overwhelm computational resources. The system requires 4 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Existing RAG methods operate in isolation retrieving either text or images without synthesizing across modalities, and this remains a challenge the framework aims to address but may not fully resolve. The paper notes that M3DocRAG performs worse with top-4 retrieval compared to top-1, suggesting difficulties in selectively integrating multiple retrieved documents.
